key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْقَيْسِ: Amir al-Qays, a title often referring to the poet Imru' al-Qays
key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الرِّضْيُ: As-Sayyad al-Radi, the compiler of Nahj al-Balagha

ai.seo_question: Who is Amir al-Qays in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi clarifies that 'Amir al-Qays' refers to Imru' al-Qays, the pre-Islamic poet renowned as the 'King of Poets,' whose works were often cited by the Imams for their eloquence despite their pagan context. This identification highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between the linguistic mastery of the Jahiliyyah poets and their theological deviation, using their verses as rhetorical tools in sermons and letters.
